subject: Re: [stan-users] How does the parameter update within a for loop

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] How does the parameter update within a for loop
parts:
There are no updates in a for loop. The sampling statements
just increment the total log density every time one is
executed.

You probably just want to use a negative binomial rather than
creating your own with a latent gamma and poisson. It'll be
more efficient, too.

- Bob

> On Nov 30, 2016, at 10:58 AM, Craig Wang <craigw...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Dear Stan users,
>
> I am trying to implement a model that estimate the reduction delta, comparing sample before events y1 and after events y2. mu is the population mean, and mub[i] is the mean of each individual before some events, y1 and y2 are samples taken from each individual.
>
> data {
> int J; // sample size
> int y1[J];
> int y2[J];
> }
> parameters {
> real<lower=0> kappa;
> real<lower=0> mu;
> real<lower=0,upper=1> delta;
> real<lower=0> mub[J];
> }
>
>
> model {
> mu ~ gamma(1,0.001); // prior
> kappa ~ gamma(1,0.7);
> delta ~ beta(1,1);
> for (i in 1:J){
> mub[i] ~ gamma(kappa,kappa/mu); // likelihoods
> y2[i] ~ poisson(delta*mub[i]);
> y1[i] ~ poisson(mub[i]);
> }
> }
>
>
> In the current implementation, delta only gets updated once for each MCMC sample, how is the likelihood computed in this case given there is a for loop but only one delta?
>
> As a result, these two dataset give the same delta estimates:
>
> y1<-c(50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 500, 500, 500)
> y2<-c(5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50)
>
> y1<-c(50, 100, 150, 200, 250, 300, 350, 500, 500, 500)
> y2<-c(275, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0,0)
>
> In reality one would expect the second dataset produce a much wider posterior distribution compare to the first.
>
>
> Thanks for any inputs!
> Craig
